concepts.why: The patient's selective acceptance of benzodiazepines and gabapentin, as well as her exhibition of catatonia-like signs and psychotic signs that seemed to be under her control, suggest factitious disorder.
The patient's history of borderline personality disorder, as well as her exhibition of unstable behavior and selective acceptance of medications, support this diagnosis.
The patient's history of major depressive disorder, as well as her exhibition of depressed mood and suicidal ideation, support this diagnosis.
The patient's history of benzodiazepine use disorder, as well as her selective acceptance of benzodiazepines, support this diagnosis.
The patient's history of opiate use disorder, as well as her exhibition of unstable behavior, support this diagnosis.
The patient's exhibition of psychotic signs, including auditory hallucinations and mouthing words, support this diagnosis.
The patient's exhibition of factitious behavior, including selective acceptance of medications and exhibition of catatonia-like signs, support this diagnosis.
The patient's exhibition of seizure-like behavior without a neurological basis, as well as her exhibition of catatonia-like signs, support this diagnosis.

rationales.F12: The catatonia specialist's evaluation suggests that the patient is unlikely to have catatonia, which rules out conversion disorder.
